triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: All eight rules of the below-floor half of the Liechtenstein pair started at 2026-02-15 instead of 2025-11-14, so heading 9903.02.88's 15 percent floor top-up did not apply during the first three months in which Annex II had inserted the heading.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 3 (li-87), the below-floor sibling; 8 effective_from changes, two effective_period proof atoms per rule citing the same FR notice, summary and corpus_citation_paths updated, no formula change. Source verified once for the whole 9903.02.82-.91 insertion (see index 3 notes).
triage.verifier_justification: The only meaning-bearing change in the module is that all eight rules' single version start moves from '2026-02-15' to '2025-11-14' (8 removed / 8 added date lines; every formula, parameter, input, output, and scope is byte-identical). The pinned corpus copy of the cited implementing notice (FR Doc 2025-23316, 90 FR 59281) states under DATES and again at the head of Annex II that the HTSUS modifications are "effective with respect to goods entered for consumption ... on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on November 14, 2025", and item 7 of Annex II is what inserts "New headings 9903.02.82-9903.02.91"; the string "February" does not occur anywhere in the notice, so the pre-fix 2026-02-15 start had no source basis and contradicted the stated effective date. Everything else in the diff (corpus_citation_paths, effective_period proof atoms, summary sentence) is provenance added to ground the corrected date, so this is a version-window fidelity correction and not a mechanical change; the date-specific kind fits better than untraceable_branch even though the old value was ungrounded, because the taxonomy assigns effective_from/version windows to wrong_period_or_effective_date.
triage.verifier_notes: Module index 4 = reciprocal-liechtenstein-9903-02-88.yaml, the below-floor (column 1-General < 15 percent) half of the li-87/li-88 pair; the commit body's F1 list names "li-87/88" among the five successor floor modules, so the quoted reason covers this file directly. Verified against the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union (corpus commit d9d6fba0, provision record e36a6a5a-a64b-506e-88c2-3ce5dad1de30, line 12 of data/corpus/provisions/us/rulemaking/2026-08-03-rulespec-tariff-rulemaking-union.jsonl): DATES paragraph and Annex II preamble both give Nov 14, 2025; Annex II item 7 inserts 9903.02.82-9903.02.91; U.S. note 2(v)(xxiv)(a) confirms the .87/.88 Liechtenstein split at the 15 percent MFN line. The HTS provision record for us/statute/hts/9903.02.88 itself carries no date, so the effective window can only come from the notice — which is why the fix also adds the second corpus_citation_path. Two caveats a reviewer may want: (1) the eight added effective_period proof atoms and the summary paragraph are provenance-only, so if a scorer weights "what fraction of the diff is meaning", this module is mostly provenance around one real date change; (2) the defect existed only on the PR 1197 branch (fix commit 4d2856a958 landed the same day the PR merged), so it was caught pre-merge rather than in shipped main. Neither caveat changes that the pre-fix encoding disagreed with the cited source. Downstream effect as the first reader described it is right: with a 2026-02-15 start, 9903.02.88's 15 percent floor top-up would have been inert for entries from 2025-11-14 through 2026-02-14.
